zubo-os.description: Rebuilt Claude Code's core loop by hand in Python: hooks, permission gates, tool dispatch, context assembly. No framework, just the loop.
zubo-os.longDescription: Zubo OS is a personal CLI agent on the Claude API that mirrors Claude Code's internals in about 300 lines of Python: a PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook system, a 3-mode permission gate (default/auto/plan), a tool dispatch dict, and a system prompt assembled at runtime from a base prompt, active skills, and a memory index. I built it to understand the deterministic infrastructure behind tool execution and context assembly, not the model.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Eira is a full-stack application for managing nursing handovers digitally. It brings SBAR handover, shift planning, clinical data and staff coordination into a single workspace, with separate flows for nurses and ward heads.

It was developed as the final project work of the degree in Informatica per le Aziende Digitali at Università Telematica Pegaso. The clinical context is fictional and there is no partnership with real healthcare facilities. Eira is an academic and demonstration project: it is not a medical device and must not be used for real clinical data or decisions.

bullets.text: Structured SBAR/ISBAR handover with priority and history.
Patient chart with vital signs, SOAPIE diary and Norton and Conley risk assessments.
Shift planning, assignments and detection of uncovered shifts.
Shift swaps with double confirmation: the colleague and the ward head.
Leave requests, hours bank and monitoring of medication stock.
Role-specific dashboards and a responsive interface for desktop and tablet.

sections.title: Architecture
paragraphs: The frontend talks to the backend through a typed client generated from the backend’s own OpenAPI schema, so the API contract is shared rather than duplicated.

bullets.label: Frontend
bullets.text: Vue 3, Vite, TypeScript, Pinia, PrimeVue and Vue Router.

bullets.label: Backend
bullets.text: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Pydantic, JWT and Alembic.

bullets.label: Persistence
bullets.text: SQLite with migrations and a non-destructive bootstrap.

bullets.label: One API contract
bullets.text: TypeScript types and the client are generated from the OpenAPI schema, and a contract check is part of the project scripts.

bullets.label: Authorization on the server
bullets.text: Access is checked per role, ward, user and shift on the backend. Frontend checks only guide the experience.

bullets.label: No known credentials in production
bullets.text: The demo seed exists only in development and end-to-end runs and is always disabled in production.

bullets.label: Tests
bullets.text: API and domain tests, component and composable tests, static checks, OpenAPI contract verification and browser end-to-end tests with axe-core accessibility checks.

bullets.label: Security
bullets.text: bcrypt password hashing, expiring JWTs with the user reloaded from the database on every request, data isolation between wards with protection against IDOR, and server-side validation of avatars.

bullets.label: Documentation
bullets.text: The repository documents the threat model and known limits in its SECURITY.md.

sections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Zubo OS is a personal CLI agent on the Claude API. I wanted to know how Claude Code actually works, so I rebuilt its core loop by hand: hooks, permission gates, tool dispatch and context assembly. That is the deterministic part of an agent, and it fits in about 300 lines of readable Python.

sections.title: The loop
paragraphs: When the model stops with end_turn the response is printed. When it stops with tool_use the loop runs the tool call and goes around again.

bullets.label: Context assembly
bullets.text: The system prompt is built at runtime from a base prompt, the active skills and a memory index.

bullets.label: Hooks
bullets.text: Four lifecycle events (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, UserInput and Stop) registered as callables on a HookRegistry.

bullets.label: Permissions
bullets.text: Three modes: default asks before guarded tools, auto allows everything and plan blocks tool execution.

bullets.label: Tool dispatch
bullets.text: Each tool module exports its schemas and functions. They are merged into one dispatch dict and called with the model’s input unpacked directly.

bullets.label: Memory
bullets.text: Markdown files with frontmatter, indexed by a MEMORY.md that is injected into the system prompt.

bullets.label: Hooks over edits to the loop
bullets.text: Logging, validation and slash commands live in hooks, so cross-cutting concerns never require changing agent.py.

bullets.label: Same skeleton, smaller scope
bullets.text: It keeps the conceptual skeleton of Claude Code and leaves out its production hardening: streaming, worktrees, MCP servers and concurrent tool calls.
